notes: *that which* goes whole to the written אֲשֶׁר under rule 46's first rider, a present relative taking its English before a supplied antecedent could be split from it; the head is left on *that* as the head of the free-relative phrase, English syntax breaking the tie under rule 24. Heading on *which*, as the token realizing the relative itself, is the competing reading.
Both פָּנֶה phrases fuse to a single *before* under rule 30's one-rendering condition (אֶל־פְּנֵי and לִפְנֵי alike), each headed on the lexeme-bearing morpheme.
וַיִּקְרְבוּ → *drew near* keeps its head on the verb under rule 44, *near* naming nothing alone.
